analysis.title: Gold's Great Unwind Is Far From Over
key_insights: Gold is breaking below the major trendline in place since 2024 and below its 100-week moving average, a level it has not traded below since late 2023. The 200-week moving average sits just above $3,000. RSI is oversold, but oversold markets can stay oversold.

The author argues the gold rally attracted speculators chasing a narrative they barely understood, and that flushing out that excess takes time. Gold still trades inside a downward-sloping channel from the all-time highs, with the lower end considerably below current levels.

ANZ estimates nearly 200 tonnes of gold have been liquidated through CME speculative positions. Net longs remain at 533 tonnes against lows around 200 tonnes in 2022 and 2023. ANZ sees scope for another 200 tonnes of speculative liquidation.

Gold volatility has started rising as spot falls, which is rare for gold. The author reads this as the crowd increasingly pricing downside fear. Reversals after parabolic, options-driven moves often bring falling volatility that suppresses deltas, as in the KOSPI AI mania.

ANZ expects Fed hikes of 25bps in December, January and March, with 50bps in December still possible. The market prices about 80bps of tightening over the cycle. Stronger US growth, sticky inflation and a resilient labour market pressure non-yielding gold.
Gold and the dollar have moved almost perfectly in opposite directions this year, so trading gold means implicitly trading the dollar.
Gold ETF holdings rose 211 tonnes in Q3, with Europe contributing 92 tonnes. ANZ warns North American ETF holdings could fall in Q4 as monetary conditions tighten.
The author argues gold is not a reliable fear hedge. Gold has sold off during several of the largest recent VIX spikes, and VIX is the better gauge of global stress.
ChiNext and gold move closely together. The author asks whether the washout in Chinese tech is forcing investors to sell gold to fund losses elsewhere, and leaves the question open.
Indian bar and coin demand fell 40% y/y to 55 tonnes in Q3. Global jewellery demand fell to 313 tonnes, the weakest third quarter on record.

ANZ raised its 2026 central bank gold purchase forecast from 850 to 950 tonnes after 321 tonnes of buying in Q3. China bought 26 tonnes in October, the highest since 2023. ANZ expects central bank buying to stay strong at lower prices, offsetting some investment liquidation.

tension_points.bull_case: ANZ raised its 2026 central bank purchase forecast to 950 tonnes after 321 tonnes in Q3. It expects buying to stay strong at lower prices, and China bought 26 tonnes in October.
tension_points.bear_case: Speculative longs of 533 tonnes could shed another 200 tonnes, the Fed is expected to hike, North American ETF holdings may fall in Q4, and Indian and jewellery demand are weak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A bear thesis would weaken if central bank buying outpaces speculative liquidation, though the report states no specific level.
